questions.stem: The LONGEST river in the world (by traditional length measure) is:
questions.explanation: Nile ~6,650 km. Amazon is close (often disputed). Yangtze is Asia's longest (6,300 km). Modern satellite re-measurements have raised the Amazon claim, but exam answers historically name the Nile.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The HIGHEST mountain in the world is Mount Everest. Its height is approximately:
questions.explanation: Nepal + China re-surveyed Everest in Dec 2020 as 8,848.86 m (up from the earlier 8,848 m). Its local names: Sagarmatha (Nepal), Chomolungma (Tibet).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The LARGEST desert on Earth is:
questions.explanation: A desert is defined by LOW PRECIPITATION, not heat. Antarctica (~14 million sq km) is a COLD desert and the largest. Sahara (~9.2 million sq km) is the largest HOT desert. Trap: most students pick Sahara.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match the strait with the countries it separates. A. Palk Strait. B. Strait of Gibraltar. C. Strait of Hormuz. D. Bering Strait. List-II: 1. Spain and Morocco. 2. India and Sri Lanka. 3. Russia and USA (Alaska). 4. Iran and Oman.
questions.explanation: Palk Strait — India (Tamil Nadu) + Sri Lanka. Gibraltar — Spain + Morocco (gateway to Mediterranean). Hormuz — Iran + Oman (Persian Gulf oil chokepoint). Bering — Russia + Alaska (USA).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Tropic of Capricorn passes through which of the following LANDMASSES? 1. Australia. 2. South Africa. 3. Chile. 4. Madagascar.
questions.explanation: 23.5° S passes through: Australia (crosses Queensland + NT), Paraguay, Argentina, Chile, South Africa (Limpopo), Botswana, Mozambique, Madagascar. All four listed are correct.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which ocean is the SMALLEST by area?
questions.explanation: Arctic Ocean ~14 million km² — smallest of the five. Size order (approx): Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The MARIANA TRENCH, the deepest known oceanic trench, is located in the:
questions.explanation: Mariana Trench — western Pacific near the Mariana Islands; deepest point 'Challenger Deep' ~10,935 m below sea level. First descended by Jacques Piccard + Don Walsh (1960) in bathyscaphe Trieste.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of country-and-capital is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Netherlands — Amsterdam (with seat of government at The Hague)
South Africa — has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town, Bloemfontein

questions.explanation: Australia's capital is CANBERRA — a purpose-built capital chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne. Sydney is Australia's largest city but not its capital. Netherlands, South Africa, Bolivia facts are correct.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The International Date Line, which marks the transition from one calendar day to the next, runs mostly through which ocean — with deliberate deviations to avoid cutting through island nations?

options.option_text: Indian Ocean, between Africa and Australia
Atlantic Ocean, between the Americas and Europe
Pacific Ocean, with bends to spare island territories

questions.explanation: The International Date Line follows approximately the 180° meridian through the Pacific Ocean. It bends east near Kiribati and Samoa and west near the Aleutian Islands to keep island groups on the same calendar day. It does not pass through the Indian or Atlantic oceans at any point.

questions.stem: The Suez Canal, inaugurated in 1869 and a pivotal route for global maritime trade, connects the Mediterranean Sea in the north to which body of water in the south?

options.option_text: Persian Gulf, the oil-rich arm of the Indian Ocean
Red Sea, enabling direct Europe-to-Asia navigation
Arabian Sea, through which tankers exit toward Asia
Gulf of Aden, the passage between Africa and Arabia

questions.explanation: The Suez Canal directly links the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea. Ships then pass through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait into the Gulf of Aden and onward to the Arabian Sea. The Persian Gulf requires further transit through the Strait of Hormuz and is not directly connected to the Suez Canal's southern terminus.

questions.stem: The Volga, the longest river entirely within Europe, does NOT drain into any ocean. Into which body of water does it ultimately empty?

options.option_text: Black Sea, which the Danube river also drains into
Baltic Sea, into which many Scandinavian rivers flow
Caspian Sea, the world's largest landlocked water body
Aral Sea, once extensive but now severely reduced

questions.explanation: The Volga empties into the Caspian Sea, which is landlocked and classified as a lake by some geographers. Confusing it with the Danube (which drains into the Black Sea) is the most common error. The Aral Sea, though also landlocked, is drained by the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers in Central Asia.

questions.stem: The Sahel is a semi-arid transitional belt running east-west across Africa, lying immediately south of the Sahara Desert. Which ecological zone borders the Sahel to its south?

options.option_text: Equatorial rainforest, as densely found in the Congo Basin
Mediterranean shrubland typical of North Africa's coast
Savanna and Sudanian woodland of sub-Saharan Africa
Temperate grasslands similar to the South African Highveld

questions.explanation: Moving southward: Sahara → Sahel (200–600 mm annual rainfall) → Savanna/Sudanian woodland → Guinea forests → equatorial rainforest. The Mediterranean shrubland lies north of the Sahara, not south of the Sahel. The equatorial rainforest is two ecological zones further south, separated by the savanna belt.

questions.stem: The Bosphorus Strait in Turkey connects the Black Sea to which intermediate sea, before ships must further navigate the Dardanelles to reach the Aegean Sea?

options.option_text: Adriatic Sea, the arm of the Mediterranean near Italy
Sea of Marmara, an inland sea entirely within Turkey
Ionian Sea, located between Greece and southern Italy
Tyrrhenian Sea, enclosed by Italy, Sardinia, and Corsica

questions.explanation: The correct chain is: Black Sea → Bosphorus → Sea of Marmara → Dardanelles → Aegean Sea → Mediterranean. The Sea of Marmara is entirely within Turkish territory and is the smallest sea in the world by some classifications. A common error is conflating the Bosphorus with the Dardanelles, which is the southern exit strait.

questions.stem: The Atacama Desert in South America is one of the driest non-polar regions on Earth, recording near-zero annual rainfall in some stations. Which combination of geographical factors BEST explains its exceptional aridity?

options.option_text: Subtropical high-pressure belt with no proximate moisture source
Rain shadow of the Andes and cold Humboldt Current offshore
Prevailing trade winds blowing parallel to the Chilean coast
High-altitude plateau suppressing atmospheric moisture capacity

questions.explanation: The Atacama owes its extreme dryness to two reinforcing mechanisms: (1) the Andes Mountains block moisture-laden easterly winds from the Amazon basin (orographic rain shadow), and (2) the cold Humboldt (Peru) Current cools the overlying air, stabilises the marine boundary layer, and suppresses convective uplift. The subtropical high-pressure belt adds a third factor but alone produces far less severe aridity, as seen in other subtropical deserts.

questions.stem: Sailors historically named three increasingly violent westerly wind zones in the Southern Hemisphere — 'Roaring Forties', 'Furious Fifties', and 'Shrieking Sixties'. In which latitude band do the 'Roaring Forties' specifically prevail?

options.option_text: Between 30°S and 40°S, within the subtropical transition zone
Between 40°S and 50°S, with minimal landmass to disrupt winds
Between 50°S and 60°S, where Furious Fifties actually dominate
Between 20°S and 30°S, inside the subtropical high-pressure belt

questions.explanation: The Roaring Forties (40°S–50°S) arise because the Southern Hemisphere has almost no large landmasses at these latitudes to disrupt the flow of strong westerly winds, unlike the Northern Hemisphere where continents break up equivalent wind belts. The Furious Fifties (50°S–60°S) and Shrieking Sixties (60°S–70°S) intensify further south. At 30°S–40°S, the subtropical high-pressure belt produces calmer conditions known historically as the 'Horse Latitudes'.
